name: Green (Pigment)
lede: Green (Pigment) is a reference value from the pigment and printing industry, a deep, saturated green closer to ink on a swatch book than to any single named shade in nature.

sections.title: A reference value, not a story
sections.body:
Our library gives this entry no deeper history than its function: it is listed as a pigment-industry reference value, one of several named variants of [[green]] alongside [[green-crayola|Green (Crayola)]] [1]. Its own source, cited only as a general web listing, does not explain who set this exact value or when [1].

The nearest named look-alikes on file are [[peppermint|Peppermint]], a shade duller, and [[green|Green]] itself, also duller [2]. [[medium-green|Medium Green]] sits almost at the same point, and [[shamrock-green|Shamrock Green]] and [[bud-green|Bud Green]] are both duller still [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries a color close enough to this one over enough of its canvas to count, as photographed [3]. A reference green built for printed pigment swatches and ink matching has little reason to turn up in painted canvases, which depend on different pigments and binders entirely [3].
